name: Telegram API for Drupal modules
description: Developer-facing service for sending messages to a Telegram bot chat, with an optional Webform submission handler submodule.

suggests.drupal/webform: Enables the telegram_api_webform submodule to post Webform submissions to a Telegram chat.

project_description: Developer-oriented Telegram integration. Provides a single service, telegram_api.service (class Drupal\telegram_api\TelegramApiService), that POSTs a message to the Telegram Bot API sendMessage endpoint. It is send-only: the module registers no routes, controllers, webhook receiver, config form, or permissions. Messages are described with a Drupal\telegram_api\ValueObject\TelegramMessage value object (text, bot token, chat_id, optional parse_mode, optional SOCKS5 proxy, optional custom endpoint URL). Two send paths exist: sendToTelegramBot() sends synchronously; queue() defers the send onto the 'telegram_api_queue' queue, drained by the TelegramQueueWorker QueueWorker on cron (or 'drush queue:run telegram_api_queue'). The telegram_api_webform submodule (requires drupal/webform) adds a 'telegram_api_handler' WebformHandler that formats a submission as an HTML message (bold webform title, per-field label/value lines, comma-separated excluded fields) and sends it to a configured bot token + chat_id. New in the 2.0.x branch: value object instead of many positional parameters, the Webform handler, custom-endpoint support, and the queue/delayed-send option. 2.0.x send example: use Drupal\telegram_api\ValueObject\TelegramMessage; $message = new TelegramMessage(text: 'Hello from Drupal!', token: '618218965:AAG...', chatId: '12345678'); \Drupal::service('telegram_api.service')?->sendToTelegramBot($message); Queue example: same construction then ->queue($message); then drush queue:run telegram_api_queue.
